questions.question: The shape of the Earth is best described as:
questions.explanation: Slightly flattened at the poles, slightly bulged at the equator.

questions.question: The two endpoints of the Earth's spinning axis are called:
options: the equator and the prime meridian
the North Pole and the South Pole
Tropic of Cancer and Tropic of Capricorn
questions.answer: the North Pole and the South Pole
questions.explanation: Geographic poles.

questions.question: How long does the Earth take to rotate once on its axis?
questions.explanation: One day = one rotation.

questions.question: Which is more accurate for showing shapes and sizes — a globe or a flat map?
questions.explanation: A globe is round like the Earth, so it does not distort.

questions.question: The main advantage of a flat map is:
options: it is easy to carry and shows details
it is the same as a globe
questions.answer: it is easy to carry and shows details
questions.explanation: Maps are convenient and detailed but distort somewhat.

questions.question: The 0° latitude line is called the:
questions.explanation: Equator is the most important parallel.

questions.question: Lines of latitude are also called:
questions.explanation: They are parallel to the equator.

questions.question: The Tropic of Cancer is at approximately:
questions.explanation: Tropic of Cancer = 23½° north.

questions.question: The Tropic of Capricorn is at approximately:
questions.explanation: Tropic of Capricorn = 23½° south.

questions.question: The Arctic Circle is at:
questions.explanation: Arctic Circle = 66½° north.

questions.question: The Antarctic Circle is at:
questions.explanation: Antarctic Circle = 66½° south.

questions.question: The North Pole is at:
questions.explanation: Highest possible latitude north.

questions.question: The South Pole is at:
questions.explanation: Highest possible latitude south.

questions.question: The hottest heat zone of the Earth, between the two tropics, is called:
questions.explanation: Torrid = hot; the sun is overhead twice a year here.

questions.question: The mild zones (between the tropics and the polar circles) are called:
questions.explanation: Temperate = mild.

questions.question: The very cold zones inside the polar circles are called:
questions.explanation: Frigid = very cold.

questions.question: India lies mostly in which heat zone?
questions.explanation: The Tropic of Cancer passes through India; most of it is in the Torrid Zone.

questions.question: The 0° longitude line is called the:
questions.explanation: Prime Meridian = 0° longitude.

questions.question: Lines of longitude are also called:
questions.explanation: Longitudes = meridians; they go from pole to pole.

questions.question: The Prime Meridian passes through:
questions.explanation: Greenwich, near London, by international agreement.

questions.question: The maximum value of longitude on Earth is:
questions.explanation: 180° E and 180° W meet at the same line.

questions.question: The 180° meridian is also called the:
questions.explanation: Crossing it changes the calendar date.

questions.question: Are all meridians the same length?
options: No, ones near the equator are longer
Yes, every meridian is the same length
No, the Prime Meridian is the longest
questions.answer: Yes, every meridian is the same length
questions.explanation: Each meridian runs from pole to pole.

questions.question: A place at (28.6° N, 77.2° E) is approximately:
questions.explanation: These coordinates are New Delhi's approximate location.

questions.question: Mumbai is at approximately:
questions.explanation: Mumbai's typical coordinates.

questions.question: Sydney (Australia) is at (33.9° S, 151.2° E). Sydney is in which hemisphere(s)?
questions.explanation: Latitude S = southern hemisphere; longitude E = eastern hemisphere.

questions.question: Place A is at 30° N, 70° E. Place B is at 15° N, 80° E. Which is correct?
options: A is north of B and west of B
A is north of B and east of B
A is south of B and west of B
A and B are at the same point
questions.answer: A is north of B and west of B
questions.explanation: 30° N > 15° N → A north of B; 70° E < 80° E → A west of B.

questions.question: City P is at 0° N, 80° W. City Q is at 0° N, 10° E. Which is correct?
options: Both are at the equator and at the same longitude
questions.explanation: Both at equator (0° N); 80° W is west of the Prime Meridian; 10° E is east. So P is west of Q.

questions.question: How much does the Earth rotate per hour?
questions.explanation: 360° / 24 hours = 15° per hour.

questions.question: India's standard meridian (used for IST) is:
questions.explanation: 82.5° E passes through Mirzapur; IST is set to this meridian.

questions.question: When it is 12 noon at Greenwich (0°), what time is it in India (82.5° E)?
questions.explanation: 82.5° east → 82.5/15 = 5.5 hours ahead of Greenwich = 5:30 pm IST.

questions.question: Two cities A and B differ in longitude by 30°. The time difference between them is:
questions.explanation: 30° / 15° per hour = 2 hours.

questions.question: How many degrees of latitude are there from the equator to a pole?
questions.explanation: Equator = 0°; pole = 90°.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a parallel?
questions.explanation: The Prime Meridian is a meridian (longitude), not a parallel.

questions.question: How many heat zones are there on the Earth?
questions.explanation: Torrid, Temperate, Frigid (with Temperate and Frigid each having a north and south half but counting as one type).

questions.question: The total number of degrees of longitude (east + west of Prime Meridian) covered around the whole Earth is:
questions.explanation: From 180° W around through 0° to 180° E covers a full circle = 360°.

questions.question: When writing a coordinate, which is given FIRST?
questions.explanation: Convention: (latitude, longitude).

questions.question: The point (0° N, 0° E) is in which body of water?
options: Atlantic Ocean (Gulf of Guinea, off west Africa)
questions.answer: Atlantic Ocean (Gulf of Guinea, off west Africa)
questions.explanation: 0,0 lies in the Gulf of Guinea, part of the Atlantic Ocean.

questions.question: The Earth is a perfect sphere.
questions.explanation: Slightly flattened at the poles — an oblate spheroid.

questions.question: A globe is more accurate for showing shapes than a flat map.
questions.explanation: Flat maps necessarily distort because they are projecting a sphere onto a plane.

questions.question: The Tropic of Cancer is in the southern hemisphere.
questions.explanation: Tropic of Cancer = 23½° NORTH.

questions.question: The Torrid Zone is the hottest part of the Earth.
questions.explanation: Sun is overhead twice a year between the tropics.

questions.question: The Prime Meridian is at 0° longitude.
questions.explanation: By international agreement (Greenwich).

questions.question: The Earth turns 15° in 1 hour.
questions.explanation: 360° / 24 h = 15° per hour.

questions.question: The 0° latitude line is called the ____.
questions.explanation: Equator divides Earth into N and S hemispheres.

questions.question: The North Pole is at ____° N latitude.
questions.explanation: Highest possible latitude north.

questions.question: The hot zone between the two tropics is called the ____ Zone.
questions.explanation: Torrid Zone.

questions.question: The Prime Meridian passes through the town of ____, near London.
questions.explanation: Greenwich, England.

questions.question: India's standard time is set to the ____° E meridian.
questions.explanation: 82.5° E passes through Mirzapur.

questions.question: The Earth rotates ____° per hour.
List one advantage and one disadvantage each of a globe and a flat map.
questions.answer: Globe — Advantage: most accurate (no distortion of shapes/sizes); Disadvantage: cannot show small details, hard to carry. Flat map — Advantage: easy to carry, can show small details; Disadvantage: every flat map distorts shapes / sizes / distances to some extent.
questions.explanation: Advantages and limitations of each.

questions.question: Name the five most important parallels and give the latitude of each.
questions.answer: Equator (0°); Tropic of Cancer (23½° N); Tropic of Capricorn (23½° S); Arctic Circle (66½° N); Antarctic Circle (66½° S). [The poles at 90° N and 90° S are also key reference points.]
questions.explanation: Five named parallels (plus poles).

questions.question: Name the three heat zones and the boundaries between them.
questions.answer: Torrid Zone — between Tropic of Cancer (23½° N) and Tropic of Capricorn (23½° S). Temperate Zones — north Temperate (23½° N to 66½° N) and south Temperate (23½° S to 66½° S). Frigid Zones — inside the Arctic Circle (66½° N to 90° N) and inside the Antarctic Circle (66½° S to 90° S).
questions.explanation: Boundaries are the named parallels.

questions.question: How would you find a city at coordinates (40° N, 100° W) on a world map? Describe the steps.
questions.answer: (1) Find 40° N latitude — count up 40° from the equator on the latitude scale. (2) Find 100° W longitude — count 100° west of the Prime Meridian on the longitude scale. (3) Trace the parallel and the meridian; the point where they cross is the location. (40° N, 100° W is in the central United States — roughly Kansas / Nebraska area.)
questions.explanation: Standard procedure for using coordinates.

questions.question: Compute: when it is 9 am at Greenwich (0°), what time is it in Mumbai (approx. 75° E)? Show your reasoning.
questions.answer: Mumbai is 75° east of Greenwich. Time difference = 75 / 15 = 5 hours. Mumbai is AHEAD of Greenwich (east is ahead). So when it is 9 am at Greenwich, it is 9 am + 5 hours = 2 pm in Mumbai.
questions.explanation: 15° per hour rule; east is ahead.

questions.question: Compare two places: A at (10° N, 20° E) and B at (10° S, 20° E). Which is north of which? Are they at the same longitude?
questions.answer: A is at 10° N and B is at 10° S. So A is NORTH of B. Both are at 20° E, so they share the SAME longitude. They are both 10° from the equator — A is 10° above, B is 10° below.
questions.explanation: Same longitude → same meridian; latitudes differ in sign (N vs S).

questions.question: Why is the 180° meridian called the International Date Line? What happens when you cross it?
questions.answer: The 180° meridian is roughly opposite the Prime Meridian. When you cross it from west to east, you 'lose' one day (the calendar date goes back one). When you cross from east to west, you 'gain' a day (the calendar date moves forward one). This convention prevents two parts of the world from having different dates simultaneously when synchronising calendars.
questions.explanation: Standard explanation of the IDL.

questions.question: A new city's coordinates are (35° N, 50° E). (i) In which hemispheres does it lie? (ii) Is it in the Torrid, Temperate, or Frigid Zone? (iii) Roughly which continent / region is this? (iv) How would the time at this city compare with India (75° E)?
questions.answer: (i) 35° N → Northern hemisphere. 50° E → Eastern hemisphere. (ii) 35° N is between 23½° N (Tropic of Cancer) and 66½° N (Arctic Circle), so it is in the north TEMPERATE zone. (iii) 35° N, 50° E is in the Middle East, roughly in the area of Iran. (iv) India is 75° E; this city is 50° E. Difference = 25° → 25 / 15 ≈ 1 hour 40 minutes. India is east of this city, so India is AHEAD by about 1 h 40 min.
questions.explanation: Complete coordinate reading: hemispheres + zone + region + time difference.

questions.question: Why does India use ONE standard time (IST = 82.5° E) even though it covers many degrees of longitude? Discuss.
questions.answer: India's longitude extends roughly from 68° E (Gujarat) to 97° E (Arunachal Pradesh) — about 29° wide, which would normally be about 2 hours of natural time difference (29° / 15° per hour). However, having different times in different parts of one country causes confusion in trains, airlines, government work and broadcasting. So India sets ONE standard time — IST, fixed at 82.5° E (Mirzapur) — for the whole country. The trade-off: in Arunachal Pradesh the sun rises about 1 hour earlier than the clock suggests, and in Gujarat about 1 hour later. Many large countries (USA, Russia) use multiple time zones; India has chosen simplicity.
questions.explanation: Explains why a single IST is used, with trade-offs.

questions.question: Using the heat-zone system, explain why countries near the equator (like Brazil or Indonesia) tend to be hotter year-round than countries in northern Europe.
questions.answer: Countries near the equator lie in the TORRID zone — between the Tropic of Cancer (23½° N) and the Tropic of Capricorn (23½° S). In this zone, the sun is directly overhead twice a year, and the angle of sunlight is always close to vertical, so the surface receives intense, concentrated heat. Countries in northern Europe (e.g. Norway, Sweden) lie in the TEMPERATE or even FRIGID zone — far from the equator. Sunlight there falls at an oblique angle, spreading the same energy over a larger area, and the seasons change drastically because the Earth's axial tilt swings the angle further across the year. So equatorial countries are hot year-round; northern countries have warm summers and very cold winters.
questions.explanation: Connects sun-angle to heat-zone differences.
